referees.quote: I broadly support publication upon adequate revision. ... Some additional data would be needed to make a convincing claim.
However, the results are indeed interesting. ... It would be helpful for the authors to more explicitly address in the main text other potential hypotheses for their data

note: No transfer from another journal is indicated; the first round is Version 0 in this file. Neither referee used a formal recommendation term, so both levels are inferred. R1 broadly supports publication but asks for substantial new experimental evidence (temperature and doping dependence), transient dynamics data, physical analysis of the oscillation period, and justification of the quadrupolar treatment, which points to major revision. R2 raises questions and asks for clarifications and added main-text discussion, without demanding new data, which points to minor revision. R2's question on whether probe averaging could explain the results could be read as stronger, but no new experiment was required. Both referees supported publication in round 2.
